business_model.assessment: Hope-Neuron is a pre-revenue, preclinical medical-device-enabled therapy company [A22]. Its product, SELtx, would draw about 300 mL of a patient's blood, treat it in a proprietary device, and reinfuse it. The company says it would do this as a 30-minute outpatient procedure. It has so far been used only in ALS transgenic mice [A22]. The planned model is recurring, per-patient therapy revenue shared with clinics and distributors: 40% to the company, 35% to the provider and 25% to the distributor. At a projected $120,000 annual price the company would keep about $48,000 per patient [A25, B3]. The payers would be patients, insurers and similar parties. The pack contains no payer, reimbursement or pricing evidence. The company also plans to partner for device placement and relies on third-party manufacturers [A25]. The 80%+ gross margin claim and the $408M–$734M revenue scenarios are management projections and depend on a human trial, FDA clearance or approval and reimbursement. None of these has been shown in the pack [A25, B1]. In plain terms, this is an early scientific bet and not yet a business with customers.

competition.assessment: The issuer says it is the 'only later-stage non-pharma solution' and has no peer with similar technology [A26]. This is an unverified issuer claim. 'Later-stage' conflicts with a therapy tested only in mice [A22, A26]. The pack itself cites competing activity: 107 active ALS interventional trials, 50+ ALS drugs in development, and three approved drugs, including Radicava and Qalsody at roughly $171k–$185k a year [A24, A26]. The issuer warns that another program's success could hurt commercialization [A26]. The pack contains no independent competitor analysis or freedom-to-operate review. The issuer lists company-owned patents (US 11471579, US 12667645, Japan), but chain of title is not documented. The risk factors also admit the company may not own or have sufficient rights to certain IP, and that patent protection is uncertain [A27]. The 'no peer' claim should be treated as unverified.

demand_evidence.assessment: There is no commercial demand evidence. Revenue is $0 in FY2025 and FY2024 [A15]. No customers, letters of intent, clinic agreements or reimbursement information are in the pack. Barrow Neurological Institute is named only as a planned trial partner [A22, A31]. The unmet medical need in ALS is described by the issuer, citing registry and ALS-organization data that the pack does not corroborate [A24]. The only scientific evidence is an issuer-described proof-of-concept mouse study at Indiana University School of Medicine, reported with p=0.008 [A23]. The pack has no study report, sample size, controls, peer review or date. The text describing the study is also truncated on page 26 [A23]. The issuer says it does not know whether mouse results will translate to humans [A23]. For a pre-revenue company, appropriate stage evidence would be reproducible preclinical data, regulatory interaction and funded trial plans. Only the first is partly claimed, and it is unverified [B1].

economics_and_funding.assessment: Financials are small and show dependence on outside funding. FY2025 (year ended 12/31/2025, about 9.5 months before the cutoff, so not stale): revenue $0, net loss $56,126, cash $19,213, total liabilities $268,348, stockholders' deficit $(249,135) [A15, A16]. Liabilities include $199,875 owed to the founder and $50,704 of convertible notes [A16, A20]. A further $150,000 convertible note was issued 6/12/2026 [A14]. The issuer reports $160,487.20 of cash at 6/18/2026 (about 4 months before the cutoff, unaudited) and claims about six months of runway. The basis is not shown, so no current runway is computed here [A18]. Notes: the two outstanding convertible notes ($60,000 + $150,000 = $210,000 face) are 2.8 times the $75,000 target [B4]. Investors would be funding a company that has already used debt that ranks ahead of common equity [A14]. At the target, 20% of proceeds ($15,000) goes to intermediary fees and $30,000 to clinical trials [A21, B5]. This is far below what a human ALS trial plus devices would plausibly need, but the pack gives no trial cost estimate [A21]. Even the $5,000,000 maximum allocates about $2.18M to trials and $635,050 to equipment [A21]. The company states the proceeds are essential to operations and that it may need more capital, so further financing and dilution are likely [A19, A10]. The company states substantial doubt about going concern in the Form C, but the auditor's report in the pack has no going-concern paragraph [A17, A19].

execution_risks.assessment: The main risks are scientific, regulatory, financial and governance risks. (1) Scientific: translation from mice to humans is unproven, and the issuer concedes this [A23]. (2) Regulatory: the therapy is subject to FDA approval, and the pack shows no FDA communications, IND or device-classification work. FDA consulting is budgeted at only $2,000 at the target [A21, A22]. (3) Timeline: the Form C says human use could begin in the second half of 2026 'with sufficient funding'. The pack has no evidence on whether this occurred or whether the offering is funded [A31, B1]. (4) Capital: the target raise is very small relative to the stated plan, and a going-concern doubt is stated [A19, B4]. (5) IP and third-party reliance: unverified patent ownership, reliance on contract manufacturers and research partners, and no agreements shown [A27]. (6) Disclosure quality: inconsistencies include XML long-term debt of $0 versus $50,704 of notes on the balance sheet, 75M founder shares 'ratified' in June 2026 versus 1 share audited, differing lock-up lengths, and conflicting statements about when the notes convert [A12, A14, A15, A11]. (7) Securities compliance: the issuer discloses a previous convertible offering that may not have complied with securities laws, with possible rescission exposure [A29].

price_and_terms.assessment: Judged separately from business quality. Price is $1.00 per share, set 'arbitrarily' with no relationship to asset value, net worth or revenue [A7]. On 75,000,001 shares this implies roughly $75.0M pre-money on basic shares [A13]. This is the price investors pay, set by the issuer, not a valuation tested by an independent investor or price discovery. The company has a stockholders' deficit of $(249,135) and $0 revenue [A16], and its therapy has been used only in mice [A22]. The pack contains no comparable valuations, so whether $75M is reasonable cannot be assessed; it should be treated as unsupported. The Form C valuation section mentions a 'valuation cap', but no cap exists in common stock, so that reads as boilerplate [A3]. Control and rights terms are weak: irrevocable 10-year proxy, custodian structure, no information rights, no anti-dilution, and issuer may change purchase limits at its sole discretion [A5, A8, A9, A10]. At the $5M maximum, investors would hold about 6.25% of shares before the intermediary's 2% shares, with votes held by the Executive Chairman [B2]. The intermediary takes at least $15,000 in cash (20% of the target) plus a $7,500 onboarding fee and 2% in securities [A6, B5]. Lock-up terms conflict (180 versus 270 days) [A11]. Existing convertible notes ($210,000 face, with $50,000 extra conversion on the second) would convert at an undisclosed price on a 'liquidity event' and dilute investors [A14]. Minimum investment is $500 [A5]. Investor-side fees are not stated in the pack [A6].

security_path_to_proceeds.assessment: The security is plain common stock, not a SAFE or note. There is no cap, discount, conversion or redemption right in the offered security [A3, A10]. Ways an investor could receive cash: (a) a sale of the company or another liquidity event, where proceeds would go to common holders only after debt and the founder payable [A14, A20, A30]; (b) reselling shares after the one-year Reg CF restriction, but no market exists or is expected [A11]; (c) dividends, which are at board discretion with no guarantee, and none are indicated [A10]; (d) a hoped-for follow-on Reg A offering into which investors would be 'converted', with no assurance [A30]. Things that usually prevent cash: no trading market, no repurchase right, shares held through a custodian as a securities entitlement, and no information rights beyond law [A9, A10]. Also, every investor grants a 10-year irrevocable proxy to Ronald Lane over all votes and written consents, so investors cannot vote on a sale, financing or charter change [A8]. Because Lane holds 100% of current shares, public investors would remain a minority with no vote even at the maximum raise [B2]. Anti-dilution protection is absent [A10]. The charter, which may set liquidation or dividend rights, is not in the pack [A10]. Most outcomes for a company at this stage involve either dilution or a loss, but the pack contains no base-rate data, so that is not quantified here.

team_evidence.assessment: Assessed on documented experience only. The founder/CEO Ronald Lane lists a PhD in Neurosciences (1973) and has led the company since December 2020, responsible for strategy, clinical studies and product development [A28]. The VP of Business Development, interim CFO and CTO list consulting backgrounds in shareholder development, interim CFO work and IT/AI [A28]. The pack documents no prior medical-device development, FDA submissions, clinical-trial management or prior company exits for management. The company says it uses contract research partners and FDA consultants, but names no clinical, regulatory or scientific advisors beyond the Indiana lab and Barrow plans [A22, A28]. This is not evidence of incompetence. It means relevant execution capability is undocumented and the key-person dependence on the founder is high, with no key-person insurance [A28, B6].

citations.quote: providing unrestricted stock, and in which the Investor would be converted into
to hold the Securities and any securities that may be issued upon conversion thereof

additional_claims.claim_text: The pack is not fully consistent that the offered common stock has no conversion element. The Form C says there is a stated interest in a later Reg A offering 'in which the Investor would be converted into'. The subscription agreement's custodian clause refers to securities 'issued upon conversion thereof'. Both look like template or aspirational language, but the pack does not show that the stock itself has no conversion feature, and the charter is absent.
additional_claims.contradictions: A3 states there is no conversion mechanic in the offered security; the quoted passages leave this open.

citations.quote: Any provision of this Subscription Agreement may be amended, waived or
hereby appoints the Chief Executive Officer and/or Chief Financial Officer of the
Investor agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Company and the Custodian and each of their respective founders,

additional_claims.claim_text: The subscription agreement allows amendment or waiver upon written consent of the majority of the voting power of the Securities. Because the Executive Chairman holds an irrevocable proxy over investors' votes, this may let him approve changes for all investors (analyst reading). Separately, each investor appoints the CEO and/or CFO as attorney-in-fact for lock-up matters and indemnifies the Company and the Custodian for breach of representations.
additional_claims.contradictions: The control effect of Section 14 together with the proxy is an inference. The pack does not say how 'voting power of the Securities' is measured.

additional_claims.claim_text: Check of the issuer's lowest scenario: 34,000 patients at 25% penetration with about $48,000 per patient to the company gives $408M. This reproduces the issuer's figure, so the arithmetic is consistent, but every input is a management assumption.

citations.quote: to achieve these estimates over a three-year ramp-up time horizon
that could be worth anywhere from 1 to almost $2 billion by 2028.

additional_claims.claim_text: Projection assumptions are optimistic given the stage. The issuer assumes the revenue estimates are achievable over a three-year ramp. The deal-page video transcript says the ALS market could be worth $1 to almost $2 billion by 2028. No human data exist, no regulatory filing is shown, and no reimbursement evidence is given.
additional_claims.contradictions: The video's 2028 market framing is not reconciled with the Form C's statement that the therapy is not yet available for human use (A22).

citations.quote: Equipment covers final engineering and the delivery of two SELtx

additional_claims.claim_text: At the $75,000 target the equipment line is $7,000, while the issuer's note says equipment covers final engineering and delivery of two SELtx devices. The pack gives no device cost, so whether $7,000 can cover this is unknown. The $635,050 equipment figure applies only at the maximum raise. Trial cost is not estimated in the pack.

citations.quote: Convertible notes payable, net of discount 50,704 -
$10,000, resulting in an initial carrying amount of
Interest Expense 4,670 -

additional_claims.claim_text: The audited cash-flow statement lists convertible note proceeds of $50,704 under investing activities. Note 5 gives the initial carrying amount as $50,000 after a $10,000 discount, so the $704 difference is non-cash accretion and not cash received. The $4,670 interest expense is not reconciled to the note terms in the pack.
additional_claims.contradictions: The reported net change in cash of $(39) reconciles only because the $50,704 is used; the true operating outflow would be about $50,000 less accretion. This is an inference from the statements.

citations.quote: The issuer represents the culmination of more than a decade of research that has
was initially registered in Wyoming on December 30, 2020 as a limited liability company.

additional_claims.claim_text: The Form C says the issuer 'represents the culmination of more than a decade of research' and says it was registered as an LLC in December 2020 and converted into a Delaware corporation in January 2025. The pack does not document how the earlier research and patents came to be owned by the issuer.
additional_claims.contradictions: Page 25 says the issuer 'controls the patents and IP critical to its process', while page 19 says it may not own or have sufficient rights to certain IP.

citations.quote: With sufficient funding and timely completion of our next-generation equipment, we believe that use in human

additional_claims.claim_text: The Form C says human use could begin in the second half of 2026 'with sufficient funding'. The 2026-10-14 cutoff falls within that period. The pack shows no evidence that a human trial, IRB approval, a trial-site agreement or next-generation devices exist as of the cutoff.
additional_claims.contradictions: Absence of evidence in the pack does not show the trial has not started.

citations.quote: This indicates a low probability (less than 1%) that the observed results occurred by random chance.

additional_claims.claim_text: The issuer characterises its p-value of 0.008 as indicating a low probability (less than 1%) that the observed results occurred by random chance. This is the issuer's interpretation. The pack gives no sample size, endpoints, blinding or replication.

issues.explanation: A3 says the offered common stock has no conversion mechanic. The pack points both ways. Page 24 says the Company wants a later Reg A offering 'in which the Investor would be converted into'. The subscription agreement (page 54) refers to 'securities that may be issued upon conversion thereof'. The Form C valuation section mentions a 'valuation cap'. These look like template carry-over, but the pack does not prove that. 'No cap, discount or conversion' should be stated as 'none found in the pack'. The charter is missing, so it is unverified.

The evidence-pack checklist lists operative_contract as present_unreviewed, price_cap_and_conversion_terms as candidate_unverified and minimum_investment_and_fees as missing. Stage A marks all three confirmed. The charter, which sets dividend and liquidation rights, is not in the pack. The conversion price of the notes is undisclosed. Investor-side fees are not stated. These should be partial or not confirmed. evidence_sufficiency should not pass in Stage D. The financial_statements item also carries unresolved conflicts (XML long-term debt of $0 against $50,704 of notes on the balance sheet).
issues.target: Critical items operative_contract, price_cap_and_conversion_terms, minimum_investment_and_fees marked confirmed_with_citation

issues.explanation: The $75.0M implied equity value rests on 75,000,000 founder shares that the board 'ratified' on 2026-06-25, about five weeks before the Form C. The audited 12/31/2025 balance sheet shows only 1 share. The consideration paid, the issue date and the board approval trail are not in the pack. The share count that sets the implied valuation is therefore poorly documented. The $1.00 price is arbitrary and no comparables are given. The valuation should be treated as unsupported, and it is not shown to be reasonable or unreasonable.

The $408M–$734M scenarios assume 25–45% penetration of all U.S. ALS patients within a three-year ramp. They also assume a $120,000 price, a partner network, reimbursement and FDA clearance, with no human data. The 80%+ gross margin claim has no cost build. The arithmetic ties to the issuer's table (C3), but the inputs are unsupported. The video also cites a $1–2B ALS market by 2028 (C4). A25 says FDA approval 'has not been sought'. The pack does not say this. It only shows no evidence of a filing.

The pack has no trial cost estimate. The statement relies on outside intuition and breaks the evidence-pack-only rule. What the pack does show: $30,000 for clinical trials at the target, $7,000 for equipment described as covering 'delivery of two SELtx devices', and $2,000 for FDA consulting (C5). The issuer says its trial may be cheaper and faster than pharma, which is unverified. The conclusion should be restated as 'trial cost unknown; the target allocation looks small and the issuer gives no cost basis'.
issues.target: A21/B economics_and_funding: 'far below what a human ALS trial would plausibly need'

issues.explanation: The pack has no base-rate data. The statement should be removed or labelled as unquantified judgment. The pack's risk factors support only that loss of the entire investment is possible and that dilution is expected.
issues.target: B security_path_to_proceeds: 'Most outcomes for a company at this stage involve dilution or a loss'

issues.explanation: Stage A omits several subscription-agreement terms. First, Section 14 lets the agreement be amended by 'majority of the voting power of the Securities'. Because the proxy holder votes investors' shares, this may mean the issuer-side proxy holder controls amendments (inference). Second, Section 7(d) separately appoints the CEO/CFO as attorney-in-fact for lock-up matters. Third, Section 6 has investors indemnify the Company and Custodian. The agreement also has a jury waiver and an exclusive Phoenix venue. These add to the weak investor-protection picture. The lock-up conflict (180 versus 270 days) is already noted in A11.
issues.target: Contract terms not covered in Stage A

issues.explanation: The Form C describes 'more than a decade of research', while the LLC was registered in December 2020 and the corporation in January 2025. Who invented and who holds title to the patents is not documented. Assignment records to the issuer are not in the pack. The risk factors also admit the issuer 'may not own' some material IP. 'Controls the patents and IP critical to its process' is an unverified issuer claim. The earlier-expiring patent bearing the higher number is unexplained. This could change the thesis, because the platform value depends on the IP.

Three descriptions of the conversion trigger conflict. Page 32 says conversion happens on a 'liquidity event'. Page 33 says conversion cannot occur before a Reg A or similar follow-on event. Note 5 defines a liquidity event as a change of control, private replacement financing or recapitalization. The conversion price, discount and cap are not disclosed. The $60,000 note was issued at a $10,000 discount, so the effective cost is higher than the 4.19% coupon. The second note carries an extra $50,000 conversion amount. Dilution cannot be estimated, and the stage-B treatment of the notes as 'senior debt' (the issuer's own words) needs the note documents.

The cash-flow statement shows $50,704 of note proceeds as an investing inflow. Note 5 says the initial carrying amount was $50,000, so $704 is non-cash accretion. The classification and amount look wrong (C6). The $4,670 interest expense is not reconciled to the note terms, and my rough estimate from the stated rates is much lower (inference). The XML reports $0 debt. The auditor's report has no going-concern paragraph, while the Form C risk factor states substantial doubt. These are signals of weak financial reporting. The audit was by a small firm, and the pack has no information on it. The $150,000 note of 6/12/2026 postdates the audit report (6/11/2026), so it is outside the audited figures.

The founder is owed $199,875 with no interest or maturity. Management has broad discretion over proceeds, and G&A (including salaries) is budgeted. The pack does not say whether proceeds could repay the founder or pay related-party compensation. The use-of-proceeds table does not list repayment. Whether any related-party compensation exists is unknown. This is a conflict of interest worth asking about.
issues.target: Use of founder payable and related-party flows

issues.explanation: The Form C says human use could begin in 2H 2026 'with sufficient funding'. The cutoff of 2026-10-14 is already inside that window. The pack shows no IRB approval, trial-site agreement, device completion or FDA contact. The next-generation devices have not been procured. Stage B treats the timeline as 'with sufficient funding' without asking whether the target raise is sufficient. It is probably not met on schedule, but this cannot be verified from the pack.
issues.target: Timeline: human use in second half of 2026

issues.explanation: The issuer reads p=0.008 as a 'less than 1%' chance the results were random and says it knows of no better ALS animal result. These are overstated and unverifiable. No sample size, endpoints, controls, blinding, replication or peer review is in the pack, and the study date is unknown. The page-26 text is truncated. Stage B correctly calls the evidence thin, but the 'p-value' wording should not be presented as strong support for the business thesis.

The pack gives only the Form C deadline of 11-27-2026 (120 days after the filing date) and no platform page, progress update or closing report. Whether the offering is open, has reached the target, has had an early or intermediate closing, or has been withdrawn is unknown at the 2026-10-14 cutoff. This is non-blocking for the research screen but is a critical item that is not confirmed.

'Only later-stage non-pharma solution' and 'no peer' are issuer claims with no independent search. Management documented backgrounds show no clinical, regulatory or device-development execution. This is a lack of evidence and not evidence of inability. The company relies on outside research and consultants who are not named or contracted in the pack. Key-person dependence on one founder who also holds all current shares, the payable and the proxy is high (B6).

briefing_ko.failure_reasons: (1) 쥐 결과가 사람에게 통할지 발행사도 모른다 [A23]. (2) FDA 승인이 필요하나 규제 진행 증거가 없다 [A22][B1]. (3) 목표액 $75,000 중 $15,000이 중개 수수료이고 임상시험에 $30,000만 배정되며 시험 비용 추정은 없다 [A21][C5]. (4) 계속기업 의문이 있고 2025년 말 자산 $19,213 대비 부채 $268,348, 자본잠식 $(249,135)이다 [A16][A19]. (5) 창업자가 CEO, 지분 100% 보유자, 채권자($199,875), 투자자 의결권 대리인을 겸한다 [B6]. (6) 특허 소유권과 경쟁 주장은 미검증이다 [A26][A27][C7]. (7) 이전 전환사채 발행의 증권법 준수 여부 의문이 공시되어 있다 [A29].
briefing_ko.future_evidence: 긍정적으로 바꿀 증거: 쥐 연구의 상세 데이터·독립 검토, FDA 사전 상담 또는 IND 관련 문서, Barrow 등 시험기관 계약과 IRB 승인, 시험 비용 추정, 특허 양도 기록, 정관과 전환사채 원문 공개, 위임장 조건 완화. 부정적으로 바꿀 증거: 공모 실패·철회, 추가 희석성 자금조달, 인체시험 지연, 연차보고서(Form C-AR)의 추가 손실·부채, 창업자 채무 상환에 자금 사용. 이 모든 판단은 불확실하며 투자 결정은 본인 몫이다.
briefing_ko.investor_proceeds_path: 이 증권은 보통주라서 만기도 이자도 환매권도 없다 [A10]. 현금을 받으려면 회사 매각 등 유동성 사건이 있거나, 1년 제한 이후 되팔아야 하는데 시장이 없고 생기지도 않을 가능성이 크다 [A11][A30]. 배당은 이사회 재량이며 기대할 근거가 없다 [A10]. 후속 Reg A 공모로 '전환'될 수 있다고 하지만 보장이 없다 [A30]. 매각 때도 회사 채무와 창업자 채무, 전환사채가 먼저이고 [A14][A20], 투자자 의결권은 창업자가 행사한다 [A8].
briefing_ko.price_and_contract: 가격 $1.00은 자의적이며 자산·매출과 무관하다고 회사가 밝혔다 [A7]. 기본 주식 75,000,001주 기준 내재 사전가치는 약 $75.0M이나 이 주식수는 감사 재무제표(1주)와 달리 2026-06 사후 승인된 것이어서 근거가 약하고 비교 가치 자료도 없다 [A12][A13]. 최대치를 모아도 투자자 지분은 약 6.25%뿐이다 [B2]. 계약상 10년 취소불능 의결권 위임, 수탁기관 보유('증권 권리'만 보유), 정보·검사권 없음, 희석 방지 없음이 있다 [A8][A9][A10]. 구독계약은 개정을 의결권 과반수로 하게 해 위임장 보유자가 영향력을 가질 수 있다(추론) [C2]. 락업 기간이 180일과 270일로 서로 다르다 [A11]. 기존 전환사채 $210,000는 전환가격 불명이라 희석 규모를 알 수 없다 [A14][B4]. 최소 투자 $500 [A5]. 중개 수수료는 $15,000 또는 $100,000 초과분 6% 중 큰 금액, 온보딩 $7,500, 주식 2%이며 투자자 측 수수료는 pack에 없다 [A6]. 정관은 없어 배당·청산 우선권은 확인되지 않았다 [A10].
briefing_ko.strongest_evidence: 발행사에 따르면 인디애나대 의대에서 ALS 유전자 이식 쥐로 개념증명 연구를 했고, 치료된 쥐가 운동 기능과 생존에서 나았으며 p값 0.008이라고 한다 [A23]. 2025·2024 재무제표는 외부 감사인의 무한정 의견을 받았다 [A17]. 다만 쥐 연구의 표본 수, 대조군, 동료 검토, 날짜는 자료에 없고 모두 발행사가 작성한 문서다 [A23][C9]. 독립적으로 확인된 증거는 없다.
briefing_ko.summary: Hope-Neuron Therapeutx는 ALS(루게릭병)를 목표로 하는 매출 없는 임상 전 단계 회사로, 환자 혈액을 장비로 처리해 다시 주입하는 치료법을 개발 중이며 지금까지는 쥐에서만 시험했다 [A22]. 보통주를 주당 $1.00에 팔며 목표 $75,000, 최대 $5,000,000이다 [A3]. 가격은 자의적이고, 투자자는 10년간 의결권을 창업자에게 위임해야 하며, 회사는 계속기업 가능성에 의문을 스스로 밝혔다 [A7][A8][A19]. 이 노트는 검토할 시간을 쓸지 판단하는 참고 자료이며 투자 조언이 아니다.
briefing_ko.unknowns: 공모가 지금 열려 있는지, 얼마나 모였는지 [A31]. 정관과 전환사채 원문(전환가격·상한) [A14]. 창업자 7,500만 주의 발행 시기와 대가 [A12]. 쥐 연구 보고서 [A23]. 특허 소유권 증빙 [C7]. 인체시험 비용과 FDA 경로 [A21]. 6개월 런웨이 주장의 근거와 현재 소진 속도 [A18]. 이전 전환사채 발행의 법 준수 [A29]. 투자자 측 수수료 [A6].
briefing_ko.what_it_does: 회사는 SELtx라는 치료법을 개발한다. 환자 혈액 약 300mL를 뽑아 장비로 처리한 뒤 다시 주입해 면역 균형을 바꾸는 방식이다 [A22]. 사람에게는 아직 쓸 수 없다 [A22]. 미래 계획에서는 환자·보험 등이 치료비를 내고, 연 $120,000 가격 중 회사가 약 40%(약 $48,000)를 가진다는 것이 경영진 가정이다 [A25][B3]. 지금은 고객도 매출도 없다 [A15].

critique_responses.response: 수용. '전환 요소 없음'을 '팀 pack에서 발견되지 않음'으로 수정한다. 정관이 없어 보통주 자체에 전환 요소가 없다는 것은 확인되지 않았다(C1). 가격·조건 항목은 확정이 아닌 부분 확인으로 취급한다.
수용. operative_contract, price_cap_and_conversion_terms, minimum_investment_and_fees는 부분 확인 이하로 보고 evidence_sufficiency를 pass로 두지 않는다. 재무제표 항목의 XML 대 감사 재무제표 불일치도 미해결이다.
수용. 75,000,000주는 2026-06-25 이사회가 사후 승인했고 감사 재무제표에는 1주뿐이어서 $75.0M 내재가치는 근거가 부실하다. 이 수치를 합리성 판단 근거로 쓰지 않고 '입증되지 않음'으로 표시한다.
수용. $408M–$734M 시나리오는 계산상 일관되나 입력이 모두 경영진 가정이다. 'FDA 승인을 구하지 않았다'는 표현은 pack에서 '신청 증거가 없다'로 고친다. 영상의 $1–2B 시장 수치도 미검증 발행사 서술이다.
수용. '인체 시험 비용에 훨씬 못 미친다'는 pack 밖 직관이므로 철회한다. '시험 비용은 pack에 없고, 목표액 배분($30,000 시험, $7,000 장비, $2,000 FDA 자문)이 작아 보이나 근거는 제시되지 않음'으로 고친다.
수용. '대부분 희석 또는 손실'이라는 문장은 기준율 자료가 없어 삭제한다. pack이 뒷받침하는 것은 전액 손실 가능성과 희석 예상뿐이다.
수용. 구독계약 14조(의결권 과반수로 개정), 7(d) 대리권, 6조 면책, 배심재판 포기, 피닉스 전속관할을 반영한다. 14조와 위임장의 결합 효과는 분석가 추론이다.
수용. '10년 이상의 연구'와 2020년 LLC·2025년 법인 등록 사이의 특허 소유권 이전 경로가 문서화되지 않았다. 'IP를 통제한다'는 미검증 발행사 주장이며, 위험요인은 소유권 미보유 가능성을 인정한다. 이는 사업 논지를 바꿀 수 있는 누락이다.
수용. 전환 시점 설명이 세 가지로 충돌하고 전환가격·할인·상한이 없어 희석을 추정할 수 없다. '선순위 채무'는 발행사 표현이며 노트 원문이 없으면 확정할 수 없다. $60,000 노트는 $10,000 할인 발행이어서 실질 비용은 쿠폰보다 높다.

수용. 현금흐름표의 전환사채 수취액 $50,704가 투자활동으로 분류된 점, $704가 비현금 상각으로 보이는 점(C6), 이자비용 미조정, XML 부채 0, 감사보고서의 계속기업 문단 부재 대 위험요인의 중대한 의문 표현을 재무 보고 품질 경고로 다룬다. $150,000 노트(2026-06-12)는 감사보고서(2026-06-11) 이후라 감사 범위 밖이다.
수용. 창업자 채무 $199,875의 상환이나 관련자 보수에 쓰일 가능성은 pack에서 알 수 없다. 사용처 표에는 상환 항목이 없고 경영진 재량이 넓다. 이해상충 확인 질문으로 남긴다.
수용. 2026년 하반기 인체 투여 가능성은 '충분한 자금' 조건부이며 컷오프(2026-10-14)가 그 기간 안에 있다. IRB 승인, 시험기관 계약, 차세대 장비, FDA 접촉 증거가 없지만 증거 부재가 미착수의 증거는 아니다. 목표액 $75,000이 충분한지는 pack으로 확인할 수 없다.
수용. p=0.008과 '1% 미만' 해석은 발행사 해석이다. 표본, 평가변수, 맹검, 반복, 동료 검토, 날짜가 없고 26쪽 설명이 잘려 있다. 사업 논지의 강한 근거로 쓰지 않는다.
수용. 공모 진행 여부는 알 수 없다. 마감일 2026-11-27은 가용성의 증거가 아니다. 연구 선별에는 비차단이지만 확인되지 않은 핵심 항목이며 evidence_sufficiency를 pass로 둘 수 없는 이유 중 하나다.
수용. '유일한 후기 단계 비의약품 해법'과 '경쟁자 없음'은 독립 검색이 없는 발행사 주장이고 마우스 단계라는 사실과 충돌한다. 팀 평가는 문서화된 이력 부재로만 서술하고 능력 부족으로 단정하지 않는다. 창업자 1인 집중(B6)은 높은 위험이다.

forecasts.outcome_definition: 2027-10-14까지 EDGAR에 Hope-Neuron Therapeutx의 Form C-AR(연차보고서)이 제출된다.
forecasts.probability_basis: 공모가 성공해 첫 판매가 있으면 연차보고서 의무가 생기지만 공모 성사 여부를 알 수 없다 [A31]. 성사되면 제출 가능성이 높고 아니면 의무가 없다는 점을 반영한 판단이다. 통계 근거는 없다.
forecasts.resolution_evidence: SEC EDGAR의 발행사 CIK 0002114933 제출 목록에 Form C-AR 또는 C-AR/A가 있는지.
forecasts.unknown_treatment: 제출이 확인되지 않으면 '미발생'으로 기록하되 공모 미성사(의무 없음)와 미제출을 구분할 수 없음을 표시한다. 조회 불가 시 '미확인'으로 둔다.

forecasts.outcome_definition: 2027-10-14까지 제출되는 Form C-AR 또는 새 Form C가 보고하는 직전 회계연도 매출이 $0을 초과한다.
forecasts.probability_basis: 임상 전 단계로 사람에게 쓸 수 없고 FY2025·FY2024 매출이 모두 $0이다 [A15][A22]. 승인 없이 치료 매출이 발생하기 어렵다는 판단이다. 통계 근거는 없다.
forecasts.resolution_evidence: 해당 Form C-AR 또는 Form C의 XML 필드 revenueMostRecentFiscalYear 값.
forecasts.unknown_treatment: 해당 보고서가 제출되지 않았거나 확인할 수 없으면 사건 실패로 세지 않고 '미확인'으로 처리한다.

criteria_applied: 모든 핵심 정보 7개 항목이 인용으로 확인되어야 pass 가능
계약 원문(정관 포함)과 증권 경제조건이 pack에 있는지
gates.uncertainty: 정관(Charter), 전환사채 조건(전환가격 등), 투자자 부담 수수료, 공모 진행 여부가 pack에 없다. 가용성 항목은 not_found_in_pack이므로 pass 불가. XML의 장기부채 0 대 감사 재무제표의 전환사채 $50,704 불일치, 창업자 75M주 발행 시점·대가 불명확도 남아 있다. 문서는 모두 발행사가 작성했고 독립 검증 자료는 없다.

criteria_applied: 무매출·임상 전 단계에 맞는 증거(재현 가능한 전임상 데이터, 규제 접촉, 시험 자금 계획)
자금 조달 규모 대비 계획의 현실성
gates.uncertainty: 쥐 실험 결과는 발행사 서술뿐이며 표본 수·대조군·동료 검토·날짜가 없다. 사람에서의 효과, FDA 경로, 특허 소유권, 시험 비용, 상환/보험 모두 pack에 없다. 팀의 임상·규제 실행 경험이 문서화되지 않았다는 것이 무능을 뜻하지는 않는다. 논지를 통과시키거나 탈락시킬 증거가 부족하다.

criteria_applied: 가격 결정 근거 및 가치 대비 합리성
gates.uncertainty: 가격 $1.00은 자의적이며 기본 주식수 기준 내재 사전가치 약 $75.0M이나, 비교 가능한 가치 자료가 없어 합리성은 입증되지 않았다. 10년 취소불능 의결권 위임, 수탁기관 보유, 정보권 없음, 희석 방지 없음, 환매권 없음으로 보호가 약하다. 정관과 전환사채 전환가격이 없어 일부 조건은 미확인이며 이 점이 결론을 바꿀 수 있으나 현재 확인된 조건만으로도 약한 구조다.
